page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.large is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a single physical core with two execution threads powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6455B processor running at a sustained clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The CPU subsystem is equipped with 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 60 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for vector and matrix acceleration including AVX-512, AMX-Tile, and AMX-INT8 instructions. The instance provides 16.0 GB of DDR5 system memory clocked at 5 GHz, delivering an 8.0 GB per core memory footprint.

The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage options for persistent file systems. Baseline networking capacity is provisioned at 1 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. In benchmark testing, the high CPU clock speed yields strong single-core performance, achieving 2214.0 in the Geekbench single-core test, single-threaded gzip compression at 34.49 GB/sec, and bzip3 decompression at 14.72 GB/sec. However, with only two virtual cores, total multi-core compute density remains constrained, scoring 2683.0 on Geekbench multi-core and registering low relative scores across multi-core stress testing and compiling tasks.

Memory bandwidth measurements demonstrate 176.26 GB/sec on small cached read operations, dropping to 18.56 GB/sec on large uncached read transfers and 17.12 GB/sec on write transfers. From an operational efficiency perspective, the instance provides high-frequency CPU cycles and a substantial DDR5 memory allocation per core, making it suitable for memory-sensitive tasks that do not require massive parallel core counts. Typical workload fits include small in-memory caches, lightweight relational databases, single-threaded ETL pipelines, and specialized enterprise services sensitive to per-core licensing.
description: Amazon Web Services r7iz.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6455B processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, providing two dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core alongside 60 MB of L3 cache and advanced instruction support including AMX and AVX-512. It includes 16.0 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. There is no bundled local storage, and the baseline network bandwidth is 1 Gbps. Performance benchmarks highlight robust single-threaded throughput, registering 2214.0 in Geekbench single-core tests and 34.49 GB/sec in single-thread gzip compression, balanced by lower multi-threaded capacity due to the low core count. The server is configured for memory-intensive workloads that benefit from high clock speeds, such as small relational databases, memory caches, and software running under per-core licensing constraints.
